Supports the onboarding team, as needed, and performs other duties as assigned. This Job Opportunity Announcement may be used to fill other Administrative Specialist GS-0301-9, GS-11 positions within the Department of Commerce in the same geographical location or local commuting area with the same qualifications and specialized experience.

This position is also advertised under EDA-OFMS-ST-26-13028546, which is open to Merit Promotion/Direct Hire/Delegated Examining eligible applicants. You must apply to both announcements if you want to be considered for both.
Qualification requirements in the vacancy announcements are based on the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards Handbook, which contains federal qualification standards.

This handbook is available on the Office of Personnel Management's website located at: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=Occupational-Series Applicants must possess one year of specialized experience equivalent in difficulty and responsibility to the next lower grade level in the Federal Service.

Specialized experience is experience that has equipped the applicant with the particular competencies/knowledge, skills and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position. This experience need not have been in the federal government.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations e.g., professional; philanthropic, religious; spiritual; community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies; knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

TO QUALIFY AT THE GS-9 LEVEL: SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: You must possess one full year (52 weeks) of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-7 level in the Federal service.

Specialized experience is defined as preparing and reviewing administrative documents, such as HR policies or forms, SOPs, office records, or personnel records, etc; AND serving as a primary point of contact for internal and external customers, addressing inquiries and resolving issues in a timely, professional manner; AND applying fundamental knowledge in administrative areas such as data entry, scheduling, timekeeping, human resources processes, records-keeping, travel, or budget and financial tracking, etc. -OR- SUBSTITUTION OF EDUCATION: Master's or equivalent graduate degree, or 2 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree, or LL.B. or J.D., if related. -OR- COMBINATION OF EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE: A combination of education and specialized experience as described above to meet 100% of the qualification requirements for this position.

Note: Only graduate education in excess of 1 full year is qualifying for combination of education and experience.

Reviewing productivity measurements for all program areas, monitors complex, challenging or problem areas and oversees implementation of solutions. Planning, organizing, and carrying out analytical studies which may impact major agency programs.

Providing advice and guidance and making recommendations regarding complex program management issues which may impact the OHC directly and the agency on a whole. Providing oversight of day-to-day operations and guidance of the branch, including supervising, mentoring, and training employees performing work at the GS-04 to GS-14 level.

Establishing program goals, objectives, workload measurements and workload standards ensuring services provided are cost-effective and meet milestones. Planning, organizing, and executing a major, substantive budget for a significant program component.

Projecting and analyzing the potential effects of budgetary actions on program viability and the attainment of resource objectives and goals. Providing authoritative interpretations of congressional legislation and DHS policies and precedents. Planning, developing, and establishing procurement objectives and contractual strategies.

Directing, performing, and/or participating in all phases of the procurement process from requirements, through contract completion. Overseeing the administration of functional contracts and is personally involved in resolving more intricate or complex problems.

## **Das kannst du bewirken** ##
* Du übernimmst die Erfassung und Kontrolle der Gebindescheine und stellst eine korrekte Datenbasis sicher.
* Monatlich gleichst du die Salden unserer Transporthilfsmittel mit Kunden, Lieferanten und weiteren Partnern ab.
* Du erstellst die Saldolisten und Gebindenachweise und kümmerst dich um deren Versand.
* Eingehende Saldobestätigungen kontrollierst du sorgfältig und erstellst bei Bedarf die Fakturierung verschiedener Transporthilfsmittel.
* Als zentrale Anlauf- und Koordinationsstelle unterstützt du interne und externe Ansprechpartner bei Fragen rund um die Salden und Prozesse unserer Ladungsträger.
* Mit Auswertungen, Rechnungskontierungen und weiteren administrativen Tätigkeiten unterstützt du einen reibungslosen Betrieb und die Weiterentwicklung unseres THM-Pools.
## **Das bringst du mit** ##
* Du verfügst über eine kaufmännische oder logistische Grundausbildung, beispielsweise im kaufmännischen Bereich, in der Logistik, im Detailhandel oder als Chauffeur oder Chauffeuse.
* Idealerweise bringst du bereits Erfahrung aus der Logistik, Spedition, Disposition oder einer vergleichbaren administrativen Funktion mit.
* Zahlen, Listen und Abstimmungen schrecken dich nicht ab - im Gegenteil: Du arbeitest gerne genau, strukturiert und zuverlässig.
* Mit den gängigen Microsoft-Office-Anwendungen gehst du sicher um und Erfahrung mit SAP ist für dich von Vorteil.
* Du kommunizierst gerne mit unterschiedlichen internen und externen Ansprechpartnern und behältst auch bei mehreren offenen Themen den Überblick.
* Du beherrschst Deutsch sicher in Wort und Schrift. Französisch- und/oder Italienischkenntnisse sind für diese Funktion erwünscht und unterstützen dich im Austausch mit unseren unterschiedlichen Ansprechpartner:innen.
## **Das bieten wir dir** ##
**5 Wochen Ferien**
Geniesse fünf Wochen Ferien pro Jahr. Ab dem 46. Lebensjahr steigert sich dein Urlaubsanspruch schrittweise auf bis zu sechs Wochen.
**Attraktive Pensionskasse mit flexiblen Sparplänen**
Unsere Emmi Vorsorgestiftung verzinst dein Altersguthaben über dem gesetzlichen Minimum. Dein Beitrag basiert auf deinem Jahresgehalt - ohne Koordinationsabzug. Wähle zwischen Standard- oder Plus-Sparplan mit 1 % höheren Sparbeiträgen.
**Freiwillige Erfolgsbeteiligung**
Je nach Geschäftserfolg erhältst du eine freiwillige Erfolgsbeteiligung. Damit möchten wir deinen wertvollen Beitrag zum Unternehmenserfolg anerkennen.
**Günstige Verpflegung im Personalrestaurant**
Für Frühstück, Mittagessen und Pausenverpflegung steht dir ein Personalrestaurant mit vergünstigten Mitarbeitendenpreisen zur Verfügung.
**Vergünstigungen**
Profitiere von bis zu 20 % Rabatt auf Emmi Produkte, attraktiven Freizeit- und Reisevergünstigungen, Sonderangeboten bei Topmarken sowie Flottenrabatten beim Autokauf.
**Kostenlose Parkplätze**
Wir bieten unseren Mitarbeitenden gratis Parkplätze am Standort.

The duties and responsibilities for a Legal Administrative Specialist (In-Court Services), GS-0901-9/11 generally include, but are not limited to, the following: Reviews legal case files for scheduled hearings to verify required documents, notices, and case information are complete and available for court proceedings.

Processes case actions during real-time court proceedings by organizing and providing required case files and supporting documents to the adjudicating official. Provides technical information on legal notices, hearing schedules, case status, and established court procedures to attorneys, parties, and the public.

Maintains official case records by processing filings, updating dockets, authenticating court documents, and retaining or archiving records in accordance with established requirements. Supports courtroom operations by preparing hearing spaces and operating video teleconferencing or internet-based hearing equipment.

Processes legal documents and case-related correspondence using automated systems to support motions, petitions, hearing notices, and other case actions. Researches case information and prepares case management reports to support the timely processing and tracking of legal proceedings.
In order to qualify for the Legal Administrative Specialist (In-Court Services) position, you must meet the following minimum qualifications: FOR THE GS-09 LEVEL: Specialized Experience: Applicants must have at least one year (52 weeks, full-time) of specialized work experience equivalent to the GS-07 level in the Federal service (or comparable experience outside the Federal service), performing 3 or more of the following duties: Reviewing legal or administrative case files to identify required documents, notices, or information needed for scheduled proceedings; Processing legal or administrative documents in accordance with established policies, procedures, regulations, or filing requirements; Providing technical information to customers or parties concerning case status, hearing schedules, notices, or procedural requirements; and Using automated case management or records systems to update, retrieve, or track case information.

(Your resume must CLEARLY demonstrate this experience) -OR- Education: Applicants must have completed a master's OR equivalent graduate degree, OR two (2) full academic years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a master's or equivalent graduate degree, or LL.B. or J.D. in a directly related field, that demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position.

NOTE: Applicants must submit a copy of their transcripts for verification. -OR- Combination of Education and Experience: Applicants must possess a combination of the above described education and specialized experience such that they total 100% of the stated minimum qualifications for the GS-09 level.

Only graduate education beyond one year, i.e., 18 semester hours, may be combined with experience under this provision. NOTE: Applicants must submit a copy of their transcripts for verification.

FOR THE GS-11 LEVEL: Specialized Experience: Applicants must have at least one year (52 weeks, full-time) of specialized work experience equivalent to the GS-09 level in the Federal service (or comparable experience outside the Federal service), performing 3 or more of the following duties: Analyzing legal or administrative case files to identify procedural issues, missing information, or actions needed to support scheduled proceedings; Applying established legal or administrative policies, regulations, precedents, or procedural guidance to resolve case-processing issues with limited supervision; Providing substantive procedural information to staff, customers, or other parties regarding case status, schedules, notices, or administrative requirements; and Evaluating case-processing issues to determine appropriate administrative action when information is incomplete, conflicting, or requires further research.

(Your resume must CLEARLY demonstrate this experience) -OR- Education: Applicants must have completed a Ph.D.

OR equivalent doctoral degree, OR three (3) full academic years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree, or LL.M. in a directly related field, that demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position.

NOTE: Applicants must submit a copy of their transcripts for verification. -OR- Combination of Education and Experience: Applicants must possess a combination of the above described education and specialized experience such that they total 100% of the stated minimum qualifications for the GS-11 level.
